result.corrected_verdict: usable_in_vigilant = NO (unchanged from the scout). ODDS: no path is both cheap and rapid. The free sandbox has no live odds; the cheapest live-odds plan is Pro at $399/mo (about $231/mo billed annually), is delayed 30 s by the vendor's own docs (no better than CNO's 13-33 s), allows only 5 books on the socket and main markets only; 'real-time' starts at Growth, $799/mo, which is CLAIM_ONLY and has no per-line age field to prove it. The hub timestamp is hub emission time, and the vendor itself says its ingest is 'polled continuously'. SCORES: the one thing that survives is a documented scores/live/{sport} socket that is not delayed and may (INFERRED only) be reachable with the free sandbox key. It cannot be tested without signing up, which this task forbids; the score source, the sports (presets show only tennis and soccer) and the age of a score at emission are all unstated; the vendor's pages contradict each other about what the free key can stream. To matter it would have to beat Sofascore's measured 2.5 s REST poll by being at least 3 s ahead of Novig's median 16 s re-quote, and a poll-fed vendor hub is unlikely to. TERMS: no terms of service exist publicly (Terms link is '#', /terms.html is 404), the free sandbox is labelled 'Prototyping integrations and evaluating the schema', display rights are stated only for Growth and above, and nothing addresses automated betting on the data; so even the free path has no licence to rely on for a live betting app. TECHNIQUE: the subscribe, buffer, snapshot handoff with sequence and event_id dedupe is sound but Vigilant already does the equivalent. Cheaper or already-owned alternatives (Polymarket and Kalshi sockets, Sofascore, ParlayAPI at $5) cover the same ground. If Tj ever wants to close the one open question, the only no-cost way is for him, not this container, to request a sandbox key and run the scores socket against Sofascore for one game; I would not spend build time before that, and the expected value is low.

details.terms_of_use: No terms of service, acceptable-use policy or API licence is published (VERIFIED 2026-10-08): GET https://surebetfusion.com/terms.html returns 404; the footer 'Status' and 'Terms' links are href="#" (home.html line 1573); the partner portal (login-gated, not entered) and consumer app bundles contain no terms/privacy text. robots.txt (VERIFIED): 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' with a sitemap, no restriction on the docs or marketing hosts; it says nothing about the API. The only licensing text is the FAQ (VERIFIED): 'Growth, Scale and High Volume include display rights inside your own product. Redistribution to third parties, white-label feeds and regional exclusivity are handled on Enterprise.' and the footer 'Odds data is provided for informational purposes. 21+.' The Sandbox card is labelled 'Prototyping integrations and evaluating the schema' (VERIFIED). Pro is pitched at 'Early-stage analytics platforms, arbitrage tools and professional bettors'. What each route would break: (1) Free sandbox inside Vigilant: outside its stated purpose (prototyping/evaluating) and no display right is stated below Growth; risk is key revocation without notice (the docs say revoked keys are closed within 30 s), not a quoted prohibition. (2) Pro $399: no display right stated, no clause on automated betting; closest fit by pitch ('professional bettors'), but unwritten permission. (3) Growth+: display rights in 'your own product' stated, still no clause on placing bets from the data. (4) The consumer app's private AppSync/socket.io backend (user-session API): never to be used; it is a private/consumer API and the project rule forbids it. Partner-portal terms, if any, are behind a login and unread.
details.free_tier_limits: Sandbox (VERIFIED on the pricing page and openapi.json): $0, 5,000 requests/day, 30 requests/min, 'Catalog GraphQL query access, Reference metadata, Pre-match odds', 'No credit card required', max 2 active API keys (x-b2b-controls activeApiKeyCaps sandbox 2), WebSocket: 1 connection, 2 books, '— (no odds WS)'. Query limits: depth 8, cost 24, 25 resolvers. Pagination: odds 20 fixtures/page, evBets/playerProps 40 selections/page, surebets 20/page; at 30 requests/min a few leagues can be polled every minute or two, or 5,000/day is about 3.5/min averaged. Live GraphQL (isLive: true) needs the 'live' scope; whether sandbox has it is not stated. Pro $399/mo (about $231/mo annual toggle): 500,000/day, 300/min, live odds WebSocket with 30 s delay, 2 connections, 5 books, 7-day trial (portal banner: 'Keep a card on file so billing continues when the trial ends'). Growth $799: 1.5M/day, 600/min, 'Real-time zero-delay', 5 connections, 10 books. Scale $1,499, High Volume $2,999. Overage $0.50 per 1,000 calls. No plan under $50 exists; the only sub-$100 prices are the consumer web-app plans ($69.99 and $99.99, CLAIM_ONLY second-hand) and those have no API.
details.websocket_or_live_included_free: Live odds WebSocket: NO on the free tier (VERIFIED docs: 'sandbox ... — (no odds WS)'; odds scope 'Pro / Enterprise only'). Live scores WebSocket: documented as gated by the 'live' scope ('Starter+', and 'Starter is scores-only'), a tier name that does not exist on the pricing page; whether the free sandbox key has it is NOT STATED (INFERRED only from the sandbox row in the WS limits table). The home page contradicts the docs by saying a free sandbox key lets you 'stream live odds from 200+ books today'. Live odds on a paid plan: Pro with a 30 s delay, Growth+ 'realtime' (CLAIM_ONLY). Player props and alt lines are never on the socket; they are POLLED over GraphQL.
details.signup_friction: Pages claim 'Free sandbox key', 'No card' and 'under a minute' (CLAIM_ONLY). Keys are issued from a tenant-based partner portal (login-gated Next.js app showing 'Welcome, <tenantName>', with /keys, /billing, /usage pages); the contact form asks for work email and company; any approval step or business-email filter is not stated anywhere I could read. I did not sign up. Pro's 7-day trial implies a card on file (portal banner). Free key caps: 2 active keys, so Tj plus the phone would fit; all signed-up tenants are B2B-framed.
details.us_sports_and_props_coverage: CLAIM_ONLY on the home page: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, NCAAF, NCAAB, WNBA, EPL, UCL, MLS, UFC, ATP/WTA, golf, each tagged 'live' with market counts, plus player props and futures. In the docs: GraphQL examples use basketball/NBA, playerProps, altLines and altProps exist (poll-only, 40 selections per page), and the channel table names tennis, soccer, basketball; the playground WS presets list only tennis and soccer. Whether NFL/NBA/MLB/NHL live odds or scores flow on the socket is not documented. Socket odds are moneyline/total/spread only, so no live props on the push path.
details.sharp_books_or_exchanges_covered: All CLAIM_ONLY: home marquee and FAQ name Pinnacle, Circa Sports, Kalshi, Polymarket, Novig, Prophet X, Sporttrade, with 200+ books; the real sportsbooks list is behind a key, so I could not confirm any of them in the live feed. Hard cap: a socket can subscribe to at most 2 (sandbox), 5 (Pro), 10 (Growth/Scale) books, so Pro cannot hold Pinnacle, Circa, Kalshi, ProphetX, Sporttrade and Novig together (6). Pregame only on the free tier. In-play odds from Pro (30 s late) or Growth+ (unproven).
details.duplicates_what_the_app_already_has: Almost entirely. Pinnacle (PinnWire/ParlayAPI), Kalshi, Polymarket (socket) and Novig itself are already read directly by Vigilant; ParlayAPI ($5), PropLine and The Odds API already supply books and props; Sofascore REST and Polymarket's score socket already supply scores. SureBetFusion sits in the aggregator/reseller tier (the same category as SharpAPI, OpticOdds, Betstamp, MetaBet that RESEARCH.md already recorded as paid or sales-gated), adds its own 30 s throttle on the only affordable live plan, and gives no per-line age. The only possibly new data (Circa, ProphetX, Sporttrade) is unverified and sits behind the $399-$799 plans. EV and surebet endpoints and the backtest simulator duplicate what Vigilant computes itself from its own scans and its scan study.
details.android_phone_feasibility: Technically yes, no server needed: plain WebSocket (OkHttp) plus JSON GraphQL POST, Bearer key, no CORS; the key would live in app settings like the ParlayAPI keys (never committed; the repo is public). Costs and risks (INFERRED from the docs): a custom protocol (hello, auth message within about 10 s, JSON ping/pong, per-client sequence and gap detection, subscribe-buffer-snapshot on every reconnect because the hub has no replay); a slow consumer is closed with 1013 and must resnapshot, which on a backgrounded phone in Doze would loop and burn GraphQL requests (20 fixtures per page); the per-key connection cap (1 sandbox, 2 Pro) can lock the app out with close 4429 if a dead connection lingers after a network switch; keys are revalidated every 30 s and closed with 4401/4403 on any entitlement change. Battery is that of one always-on socket plus message volume on main markets of up to 5-10 books. Network: from this container every SureBetFusion host that serves docs, marketing, portal or app returned 200, so there is no evidence of a block; api.surebetfusion.com and wss://events.surebetfusion.com were NOT probed (key required), so nothing is known about reachability from the phone either way. Not recommended: not worth the build at $399+/mo or on an unlicensed free key.

contrary_evidence.what: The developer docs are unusually detailed and internally consistent (AsyncAPI 2.3.0 with per-client sequence, event_id idempotency, forced key revalidation every 30 s, explicit close codes), which looks like a real engineered hub rather than vaporware. This is the best point in its favour.

The docs state that scores.* events are never delayed (only odds.* are on Pro) and that scores need only the 'live' scope ('Starter+'), and the WS limits table has a sandbox row with 1 connection, so a free scores socket is plausible. Not proven; the pricing page lists no live access for Sandbox.

The home page says a free sandbox key will 'stream live odds from 200+ books today', which, if true, would be better than the docs say; but it contradicts the docs and the Sandbox pricing card, so it is not reliable.

Pro includes a 7-day trial, so a time-boxed measurement of the 30 s-delayed odds socket is possible at no charge (a card on file is implied by the portal banner); that would only test the delayed tier and is not allowed in this task (no sign-ups, no payments).

No third-party review, forum thread, GitHub issue or independent latency measurement of SureBetFusion exists in the two web searches I ran on 2026-10-08, so there is also no independent evidence that it is slow; its speed is simply unmeasured.
